issues.detail: Clearwater Analytics' take-private by Permira/Warburg Pincus (with Francisco Partners, Temasek) closed 2026-06-25. All shares were converted to $24.55/share cash (~$7.4B total consideration); CWAN is delisted from NYSE. portfolios.json still lists CWAN as a live Growth-sleeve holding, over 5 weeks after the position actually converted to cash. The Alpaca quote feed is still returning a price (~$24.56, essentially frozen at the deal price) for the delisted ticker, which is a data artifact, not a live market — this run mapped CWAN using that frozen quote for continuity but it should not be treated as a tradable equity going forward.

summary.headline: First-run Sentinel: CWAN take-private closed 6+ weeks ago but portfolios.json still lists it as a live position — roster needs correction. NTR and OKE both down on analyst downgrades (secondary-source only, not yet tier-1 confirmed). AMD reports Q2 after today's close — first hyperscaler capex read of the season.

flags.headline: NTR down 4.5% on a Jefferies downgrade, with Q2 earnings landing tomorrow (Aug 5)
flags.detail: Nutrien fell 4.5% in the 2026-08-03 session after Jefferies analyst Laurence Alexander cut the stock to Hold from Buy, slashing his price target to $63 from $96 on demand/supply risk beyond this year. Q2 2026 results are scheduled for 2026-08-05 (tomorrow), so some of the move may also be pre-earnings de-risking. Sourced via secondary aggregators (GuruFocus, QuiverQuant) reporting the Jefferies action, not a primary release — treating as AMBER rather than RED per the tier-1 evidence rule until a wire/primary source confirms the rating change and its rationale.

flags.headline: OKE down 2.8% today, extending a downgrade-driven slide on growth-deceleration concerns that matches a listed key_risk
flags.detail: ONEOK fell another 2.8% in the most recent session (to $88.23) amid continued pressure from Morgan Stanley (cut to Equalweight from Overweight, PT to $103 from $113) and Jefferies (cut to Hold from Buy) downgrades citing a less clear post-2026 growth path and rising capex needs. This directly matches OKE's own screener report key_risk: '2026 EPS guidance midpoint is only 2% above 2025, with major growth projects not contributing meaningfully until 2027-2028' and 'Forward PEG of 2.18 implies growth expectations current guidance doesn't support.' Exact dates of the downgrades themselves are not pinned down precisely (secondary-aggregator sourcing only), so held at AMBER rather than RED pending tier-1 confirmation, but flagging the thesis match as the notable part.
flags.thesis_link: Matches OKE key_risk: 'Growth deceleration — 2026 EPS guidance midpoint of $5.53 is only 2% above 2025's $5.42, with major growth projects not contributing meaningfully until 2027-2028' and 'Forward PEG of 2.18 implies growth expectations that current guidance doesn't support.'

flags.headline: CRDO +5.4% — today's biggest mover, on continued AI-infrastructure demand and bullish sell-side action
flags.detail: Credo Technology led the book's movers, up 5.4% to $218.32. No adverse news; move consistent with the broader AI-infrastructure connectivity cycle and recent bullish analyst action (BofA raised its price target to $340 from $252, Buy; Evercore ISI initiated at Outperform, $325 PT). Catalysts on track, thesis intact.
